To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) Vampire is the most powerful ATP for the certification of aerospace software, (ii) Vampire is the fastest ATP for the certification experiments, (iii) Spass is the second most powerful ATP for our experiments, (iv) e-setheo is the second fastest ATP for our experiments.
the use of ATPs is a viable approach to the automated certification of software and that the use of rewriting is essential to the success of this approach.

the use of a rewriting system to preprocess and simplify proof obligations is a key enabler of full automation in software verification, and that the choice of the ATP has a major impact on the success of the verification process.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a novel application of ATP technology to the certification of software and the development of techniques for improving its performance in this application.
the application of automated reasoning to the verification of safety critical software.
the use of ATPs in an industrial setting, where they are expected to perform well and to be reliable.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Vampire is the most successful system in this context, but that the performance of all three systems is very similar.
Vampire is the best ATP for our application, followed by Spass.
e-setheo is best suited for the preprocessing stage, Spass is best suited for preprocessing and proof search in conjunction with e-setheo, and Vampire performs best in the proof search stage.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the ATPs are able to solve a significant number of the proof obligations, but that they are also unable to solve a substantial number.
Vampire and Spass perform best in the first simplification stage, whereas Vampire and e-setheos perform best in the second simplification stage.
the ATPs are able to solve 80-95% of the tasks, but that the success rate varies significantly across tasks and ATPs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the preprocessing steps, which are implemented using a combination of rewriting and term rewriting, are essential in making the certification process fully automatic.
the use of an ATP for certification purposes requires the use of an efficient and flexible ATP, and the use of an aggressive simplifier.
the ATPs can solve the majority of the proof tasks, but that they are sensitive to the quality of the preprocessed proof obligations.
